I didn't write the FAP. A stock Flipper on official firmware 1.5.1 can't control this kettle on its own, so any code would have called functions the firmware doesn't provide. I haven't built anything or tried it on a device. The Flipper-side finding rests on the project's pinned source notes for 1.5.1 (read, not tested), and I didn't re-check the firmware source myself.

**Why it doesn't work:** the kettle is a BLE peripheral, so the Flipper has to act as the BLE central. That means scanning, connecting, finding service `ff00`, writing `ff01`, enabling notifications on `ff02` and bonding. On 1.5.1 the Flipper's Bluetooth is set up as a peripheral only. None of the scan, connect, service-discovery or write-to-device calls are available to a FAP. The Bluetooth functions it does have only let it act as a server, and a custom server doesn't change that. This is a limit of the public API, not of the radio chip.

**What I'd suggest:** keep the Flipper as the remote, but add a small BLE-capable board (for example an ESP32 or nRF52) on its GPIO header. The Flipper app handles the on/off and 40–100 °C screen and talks to the board over UART. The board handles the Bluetooth side. That keeps "no phone". The other routes are a computer doing the Bluetooth, or a custom-firmware project, which isn't a FAP.

Before I can build anything I need three things from you:
- **Route:** which of those options you want, and which board you own if it's the add-on board.
- **Checksum:** `kettle-protocol.md` doesn't say how the frame's last byte is calculated.
- **Pairing:** the notes don't say what the first-time bonding needs, such as a passkey or just-works.

The full write-up is in `/tmp/fred-eval/pilot/518e6eec14/ws/compatibility-card.md`.
